record.title_md: [Open problem: removing diameter dependence from Theorem 1.1](https://arxiv.org/abs/1705.02166)

dossier_meta.catalog_title: Open problem: removing diameter dependence from Theorem 1.1
dossier_meta.statement_text: Can the dependence on the diameter $R$ be removed from Theorem 1.1? That is, does there exist a function $f(n)$, independent of the diameter of $K$, such that $E^n \not\to (\ell_2, K)$ for every $1$-separated set $K \subset E^n$ with $|K| > f(n)$?
dossier_meta.context_text: Theorem 1.1 requires $|K| > 10^4 n \log R$ where $R$ is the diameter of $K$. The authors note in the concluding remarks that a complete answer to the Erdős et al. problem on a universal two-coloring bound would follow from resolving this problem, and describe it as interesting in its own right.
